_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). ALMOST PURE ROCK, WATER AND SEALS -- there is NO FOLIAGE IN THIS TILE AT ALL, and none has been invented. This is the bottom-left corner of the whole scroll: the river mouth opening out, the great diagonal rock ridge coming down from the upper right, a scatter of boulders standing in still water, and the collector's seal column stacked down the left margin over bare silk. A colour test confirms the judgement: zero pixels in the entire tile are cooler than the silk ground (no green, no blue-green), whereas the neighbouring t005 has a clear blue-green orchid tuft. The ochre wash on the ridge at the top right is ROCK WASH, not autumn leaves -- at 4x it resolves into long parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes following the stone's fall line, with dark 点苔 moss dotting along the ridges. The dark caps on the small midstream boulders are moss dots too. If a mask ever lights up in this tile, the mask is wrong.

objects.name: the broad still water of the river mouth filling the tile
objects.note: mostly bare silk (留白) -- the water is DRAWN only as fine ripple lines curling around each boulder, at the top-left, around the mid ledge, beside the right-hand rocks, and under the big foreground rock at the bottom. The lines ARE the water: they travel as a surface, never as cards. The large empty middle and lower-left, where the seals sit, is unmarked silk and must be treated as the same still plane -- do not read it as void and do not put ripples there that the painter did not draw

objects.name: the great diagonal rock ridge falling from the top-right
objects.note: THE TRAP IN THIS TILE. It carries a pale ochre/yellow wash that at thumbnail size reads as autumn foliage; at 4x it is unmistakably 牛毛皴 -- long parallel hair-like strokes running down the slope's form, with dark moss dotting along the crests. There is no green, no leaf glyph, no stem, no branch. NEVER animate
